deities: Shantadurga (Santeri, chief deity - goddess who mediates between Shiva and Vishnu)
three smaller temples of associated deities on three sides

history.dynasty: Maratha (built under Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj's reign; Goud Saraswat Brahmin community)
history.summary: The original temple stood at Quelossim (Keloshi) in Salcete and was destroyed by the Portuguese in 1566; the idol was shifted via Cuncolim to Kavalem (then under the Bijapur Sultanate). A mud shrine was established in 1728, and the current temple was constructed 1713-1738 under Maratha king Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj of Satara (grandson of Shivaji), through minister Naroram Rege; Baji Rao I bequeathed the village of Kavalem to the temple in 1738. Renovated in 1966. On 4 December 2016 the devasthan completed its 450th year of existence - a count that traces the deity's continuous worship from the original Quelossim temple, not the 18th-century structure (flag as potential confusion). Shantadurga, shown holding two serpents symbolising Shiva and Vishnu, is the Kuldevi of many Goud Saraswat Brahmin families; the Kavale Math swamiji is its spiritual head. CSV town correction: the temple is at Kavalem, Ponda (North Goa), NOT Vasco da Gama as the CSV claims.

name: Shree Shantadurga Temple
town_description: Kavalem is a village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, about 30 km from Panaji at the foothills of the Western Ghats. It lies in Goa's famous temple belt, where deities displaced from Portuguese-ruled Salcete were re-enshrined from the 16th century onward.
tradition: Hinduism (Shakta; Kuldevi of Goud Saraswat Brahmins)
